issue.title: Losing invalid token message if a write exception occurs

repository.name: pushy
repository.description: A Java library for sending APNs (iOS/macOS/Safari) push notifications

body:
Experiencing same problem here... (non-netty) server definitely writes X bytes of fixed length data, but in the handler of my FixedLengthFrameDecoder I get a ByteBuf with 0 readableBytes().

This happens randomly.

Reproducible with test com.notnoop.apns.integration.ApnsConnectionCacheTest#cacheLengthNotification()

of branch "netty" in fork https://github.com/flozano/java-apns (trying to rewrite ApnsClientImpl with netty).

In this test, ApnsResultDecoder sometimes receives ByteBuf with readableSize()==0

When SslHandler is in the pipeline it happens all the time. And withound SslHandler this issue occurs too, but not so often. At least in my project this regularity is constantly.
The problem I discovered is that on a write exception netty will close the socket with bytes to be read on the socket.  Once closed, those bytes are lost.

Can you point me to the code where it „just close“ the socket ?

Am 30.10.2013 um 20:50 schrieb andrewscode notifications@github.com:

> The problem I discovered is that on a write exception netty will close the socket with bytes to be read on the socket. Once closed, those bytes are lost.

I was able to solve the problem by calling ((NioUnsafe)future.channel().unsafe()).read() inside the operationComplete method of a write listener if the future had a exception cause.   This forces netty to read from the socket before it closes it.

One last note,  this is for linux.  Windows has a bigger issue that if one tries to write to the socket and windows thinks its closed (RST packet arrives),  then windows "may" not let you read from the socket.   Works fine in linux though.
I'm not sure what the correct answer is for everyone... maybe some people don't want that data.  I know that for the apple push notification protocol,  that data is crucial.
@andrewscode could you try to build a snapshot from https://github.com/netty/netty/tree/write_close_fix and see if it fix your problem ?

Which is?

I've tried out the build, and it fixes the read problem but it causes another synchronization issue.

The problem that I have is as follows:

1.) Write to netty:
`ChannelFuture writeFuture = this.channel.write( notification );`
2.) Flush and wait for write to finish

```
    this.channel.flush();
    writeFuture.await();
```

3.) At this point in time, I determine from the writeFuture that a write exception occurred and I want to close the channel and open a new one.  But I need those bytes read before I close the channel.  Now I could wait on the closeFuture instead of calling close, but that assumes netty will close the socket.  Is there a possibility of providing information to the future that the channel is intending to be closed?
Why you could not just add a ChannelFutureListener to the write future and check if it was failed because of a IOException. If so not close it as it will be closed later and if not close it.

That's what I was trying to mention in the above post, but we thought it was too dependent on internal netty code.  For instance, what guarantee is there that the socket will always be scheduled to be closed on a write error?  Maybe a future version of Netty will stop doing that.

Another option is the ability to configure auto-closing on a write exception.   If we could turn that off,  then we could solve this problem in a cleaner way.

Yeah I agree… 

Have you depend on internals is not a good idea. Let me think about this in more detail.
